title: Cold stress effects on exposure tolerance and exercise performance
population: Review of human cold tolerance and exercise performance in cold air and water
findings: Cold weather can have deleterious effects on health, tolerance and performance.
The impact of cold exposure on physical performance, especially aerobic performance, has not been thoroughly studied; the few studies suggest aerobic performance is degraded in cold environments.
Proposed mechanisms: decreases in deep body and muscle temperature, and changes in cardiovascular function and metabolism.
Strength and power are also degraded during cold exposure, primarily through a decline in muscle temperature.
Thermoregulatory fatigue (reduced shivering and vasoconstriction after multistressor factors including exhaustive exercise) is described.
limitations: Narrative review; sparse running-specific evidence; mostly cold-water and military contexts; no numeric thresholds in the abstract.
implications: No numeric cold-side pace penalty is justified by this review; add a generic cold-weather advisory (warm-up, layering) and treat any cold-side slope borrowed from Mantzios 2022 as unverified.
Flag very long, slow ultras in cold conditions for extra caution (inference from thermoregulatory fatigue, not a stated finding).

verification.notes: Crossref (Compr Physiol 2015-12-15) and Europe PMC abstract re-fetched. Europe PMC lists Tipton twice in the author string; Crossref has Castellani and Tipton. The last implication is an inference, labelled as such.
